hints.title: Read the moduli as distances
hints.body: For each absolute value, mark the number it measures distance from. Pay attention to the plus signs inside the moduli.
hints.recap: The modulus of a difference is the distance between the two numbers.
hints.pause: Mark the fixed numbers on a number line.

recall.reminder: The modulus of a difference is the distance between the two numbers.

hints.title: Find the two boundaries
hints.body: For each inequality, find the midpoint between its two fixed numbers. Test which side is closer to the required number.
hints.recap: Midpoints give equal-distance boundaries; test either side to solve a distance comparison.
hints.pitfall: The equality point is excluded by a strict inequality.
hints.pause: Write the solution interval for each comparison.

recall.reminder: Midpoints give equal-distance boundaries; test either side to solve a distance comparison.

hints.title: Keep only the overlap
hints.body: Draw both solution intervals on the same number line. Only their shared part satisfies both inequalities.
hints.recap: AND means both statements must hold together.
hints.pitfall: Both conditions must hold for the same x.
hints.pause: Find the overlap and use its endpoints to calculate its length.

recall.reminder: AND means both statements must hold together.

solution:
The inequality |x+5|<|x+11| says that x is closer to −5 than to −11. The midpoint is −8, so it requires x>−8.

The inequality |x+11|<|x+1| says that x is closer to −11 than to −1. Their midpoint is −6, so it requires x<−6.

The intersection is −8<x<−6, an interval of length 2. Answer: D.
knowledgePattern: Translate distance comparisons into intersecting number-line intervals
